facts.statement: Anarthraspis was an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm fish that lived during the Early Devonian period.
facts.quote: Anarthraspis is an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm fishes which lived during the Early Devonian period.

facts.statement: The two species of Anarthraspis were described in 1932 and assigned to the genus in 1934, with fossils found in the Beartooth Butte Formation of Wyoming and Montana, USA.
facts.quote: It contains two species described in 1932, Anarthraspis chamberlini and Anarthraspis montanus, both found in the Beartooth Butte Formation of Wyoming and Montana, USA, and assigned to the genus in 1934.

facts.statement: The type species Anarthraspis chamberlini lived at the same time as the placoderm Bryantolepis.
facts.quote: The type species, Anarthraspis chamberlini, was a contemporary of the placoderm Bryantolepis.

facts.statement: The species name chamberlini honors British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain.
facts.quote: The specific epithet, chamberlini, honours British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain.

facts.statement: The parent group of Anarthraspis is the family Actinolepididae.
Anarthraspis belongs to the class Placodermi.
Anarthraspis lived between 410.62 and 393.47 million years ago during the Emsian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Emsian to Emsian (410.62 to 393.47 million years ago)
